_names: Terminologia Anatomica individual terms (explicitly public domain)
_definitions: Written for this module in the register of Gray's Anatomy 1918 (PD-US); NOT a verbatim quotation.
_geometry: Classical segmentation, NO machine learning and NO licensed model: atlas-pipeline/segment_hand_ct.py on Visible Human frozenCT slices 1800-1890, at a 600 HU cortical threshold.
_only_one_structure_and_why: This module labels ONE group, `hand-bone`, and that is a deliberate limit rather than laziness. The FOOT could be split into tarsal, metatarsal and phalanx because the cadaver's feet are plantarflexed: their long axis runs along the body axis, so body-axial slices cut them proximal to distal and the three groups fall into z-bands separated by clean gaps. The hands do not lie that way - they rest flat against the thighs and the whole hand occupies only VHP 1805-1885, about 8 cm, which is a hand's WIDTH not its 19 cm length. Axial slices therefore cut ACROSS the hand and no z-banding exists.
_two_failed_attempts: Both recorded because both failed. SIZE: at 600 HU the 21 components span 1180-2681 voxels, near-uniform - a carpal, a metacarpal and a phalanx are not separable by volume here. PCA along each hand's own long axis: projected centroids gave scattered gaps (23.0, 7.3, 7.5, 15.9, 26.3, 18.5, 6.1, 23.3, 0.7) with no three-band structure, and the dominant axis returned was contaminated by the left/right split used to separate the two hands in the first place. Naming individual carpals needs articulation-based matching, which needs the licensed `appendicular_bones` model or hand-authoring.
_the_600_hu_finding: Same as the foot. At 250 HU the hand skeleton fuses into 8 blobs (28323 and 25661 voxels among them). At 600 HU - cortical bone only - it separates into 21 individually sensible bones. A hand pair has 54 bones, so this is an acknowledged SUBSET limited by the 8 cm crop and the 200-voxel floor, not a mislabelling.
_why_no_sides: No side is asserted, consistent with every other module.

hand-bone.name: Bone of the hand
hand-bone.definition: The skeleton of the hand comprises the eight carpal bones of the wrist, five metacarpals, and fourteen phalanges - two in the thumb and three in each of the other digits.

_why_caps: A single cut crosses many small hand bones at once; identical repeated labels saturate both gutters.
